rules.body: Apply when persistent buffered work outlives its current observer and saving can synchronously navigate. README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate." docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription."

Route edits through the existing document task keyed by document identity. Each edit replaces pending text and restarts the 120 ms interval; quiet expiration saves the latest text once. Keep the task reusable for later bursts. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save."

Keep persistence responsibility in the coordinator dictionary independently of subscription retirement. When open, close, or dispose leaves a document, flush its pending text before departure returns instead of canceling or abandoning it. This preserves edits previously written immediately. TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." src/coordinator.js: "edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}" and "close(){++request;retire();},dispose(){api.close();}"

Finish retiring the departing view before flushing: detach current navigation state, stop its subscription, and complete departure rendering before invoking a save that can navigate synchronously. After flushing, check the opening operation's navigation authority before installing or rendering its requested view. A nested navigation must remain authoritative. docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." README.md: "Save callbacks can synchronously navigate."

Consume a snapshot of pending text and clear the old timer and pending state before calling the store. Preserve the existing utility's ordering and reuse behavior, including valid empty text. src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };" and "const retire = () => { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); ticket = null; value = null; };"

Preserve workspace methods, document identities and text, current-document rendering, subscription cleanup, and status payload semantics. docs/host-api.md: "createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide()." and "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics."

Keep the adjacent preview's separate transient policy: 40 ms trailing publication, hide cancellation, and later reuse. Do not generalize document departure flushing to preview hiding. TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Use controlled timers and synchronous store listeners to verify source obligations: no write before 120 ms of quiet, one latest-text write afterward, another successful burst, empty-text persistence, and persistence before open/close/dispose returns. During departure saving, synchronously invoke open or close and verify the older operation cannot overwrite that navigation or its rendering. Verify reopening retains saved text and preview still publishes after 40 ms, discards hidden pending work, and accepts later queries. These checks derive from TASK's "Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." and docs/host-api.md's "Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled."

limitations: Applies to persistent document work owned by a coordinator dictionary; a boundary that explicitly discards pending work requires a different policy.
The task does not define exception recovery for throwing host callbacks or navigation reentry from arbitrary host callbacks.
Attempt 1 reports passing observations, but one passing implementation does not prove causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit on other tasks.
Static AST findings and automatic contracts are review guidance, not independent requirements. No scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests were accessed.
